advisor_identified: Stephen John Harris, military historian at the Directorate of History and Heritage and adjunct research professor of history at Carleton University.

doctorate.title: Canadian Brass: The Growth of the Canadian Military Profession, 1860-1919

evidence.says: Alexander Angus Babcock’s Carleton history dissertation, dated December 2008, matches the first student title. Its acknowledgements (p. iii) identify Stephen Harris and Norman Hillmer as the two thesis supervisors; it also cites Harris’s Canadian Brass.
The History section lists S.J. Harris among adjunct research professors, with BA and MA from McMaster and PhD from Duke. The calendar identifies the listed faculty as approved graduate supervisors.

The Stephen John Harris Fonds biography states that he began doctoral studies at Duke University in 1974 and completed his PhD in 1979. It identifies him as Chief Historian at the Directorate of History and Heritage and links his thesis to the published Canadian Brass.

The defence library catalogue (call number UB 147 H3) records Stephen John Harris’s Canadian brass: the growth of the Canadian military profession, 1860-1919 as a PhD thesis, Duke University, Department of History, 1979.

notes: Institution, year, department and dissertation title match linked AHA record 27163. The later book is titled Canadian Brass: The Making of a Professional Army, 1860-1939; the doctorate title above follows the separate thesis catalogue entry.
